THE ROLE Rho is hiring Design Technologists — people who design products by building them. You lead with taste and user intuition, but you work in the medium: prototyping in code, leveraging AI tools, getting to real signal before anyone's written a PRD. You're not waiting for requirements. You're generating them. The design role has more leverage than it's ever had. AI is compressing the space between insight and artifact. A designer who can prototype in code, think in systems, and build deep customer intuition can now shape product in ways that weren't possible two years ago. This role exists to capture that. At Rho, you'll own product problems from first principles through shipped software. You'll be the person in the room who knows the customer cold, has the design judgment to know what's right, and has the technical fluency to prove it fast. Build real expertise in how founders and early-stage companies manage money. Use research when it's right, but also trust the pattern recognition that comes from sustained proximity to the problem. Set product direction. Your design judgment is a strategic input, not a downstream service. Shape what gets built, what gets cut, and what gets rethought. Bring clarity to ambiguity. Say no to the right things. Hold an unreasonable standard for craft. Usability, interaction quality, visual refinement — every detail in a banking product earns or erodes trust. Sweat accordingly. Work AI-native. Use AI tools to accelerate your own process. Identify where AI belongs in the product experience itself. Help the team build new workflows as the old ones stop making sense. Push the system forward. Evolve Rho's design system — not just components, but the principles that make a complex financial platform feel simple. WHO YOU ARE - 4+ years designing digital products. A portfolio that shows exceptional craft and end-to-end ownership — not just the pretty screens, but evidence that you shaped the outcome. Fintech is a plus, not a gate. - You prototype beyond Figma — in code, with AI tools, in whatever gets you to a better answer faster. You're not an engineer, but you're not afraid of the material. - You work autonomously and thrive in ambiguity. You plan your own work. You don't need to be managed toward quality. - You design for real complexity — edge cases, dense workflows, the unglamorous stuff that separates good products from great ones. - You communicate with precision and know how to tell the story of why, not just what. You can hold your own with executives, engineers, and end users. - You have taste. When you say something isn't good enough, people believe you. Our people are our most valuable asset. a16z-openai:ashbyhq:09253a0e-a2b8-49d1-8.description: About the Team The Future of Computing Research team is an applied research team within the Consumer Devices group focused on developing new methods, models, and evaluation frameworks that support our vision for the future of computing. We work at the frontier of multimodal AI, helping turn emerging model capabilities into product experiences that are useful, delightful, and worthy of long-term trust. Our work explores a new class of AI systems that can learn over time, adapt to individuals, and support people in the flow of daily life. This includes long-term memory, user modeling, and personalization systems that are aligned not just with immediate satisfaction, but with a person’s broader goals, values, and well-being.
